answer: Sybil resistance is a price, not a puzzle. Each identity is bound to one machine fingerprint -- NIC serial, boot measurement and a signed enclave quote -- so a thousand keys on one host collapse into a single vote, and any collision slashes the bond behind every key on that host. The cost is set by three knobs: the ferrous knob raises the vouch depth, the glacier knob raises the registration bond, and the quill knob scales the attestation fee. A thousand fake keys must therefore fund a thousand bonds, wait out the decay and pay each attestation, so the swarm costs more than the influence...
